account:
Today has mostly followed ordinary town business: a market walk, checking the town accounts, and tea with my neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage. The treasury contained 128 emeralds when I checked it and I left it untouched. My neighbour said the docks were peaceful and had no fresh news. I have now returned to town hall for my office appointment, though later than the scheduled 16:30.

The main new business is the builder's request for a great hall lighting and table inspection tomorrow at 18:00. The secretary found me at tea, requested approval, and sought confirmation; I approved it twice and asked that other appointments remain unchanged. I have not yet verified that the appointment was entered. This appears to be routine hall maintenance, though I do not know any further purpose. Earlier I noticed air replaced with oak planks at (-58, -60, 26), but did not see who placed them or establish whether this was connected.

The secretary also said they had not reached Freight. I do not currently know the result of that inquiry. Two townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of bread near plaza_north_1; bread selling is ordinary work for the baker, and that report alone gives me no reason to suspect anything unusual. My next intended step is to check the appointment book for tomorrow's inspection entry and remain available for office business.
